question: A, B and C invest a sum in the ratio of 61 : 43 : 90, respectively. If they earned a total profit of ₹2,910 at the end of the year, then what is the difference between share of B and C?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time of investment is the same, profit is distributed in the ratio of investments.

Difference in ratio of B and C = 90 − 43 = 47 parts.

Total profit ratio = 61 + 43 + 90 = 194 parts.

Difference = (47 ÷ 194) × 2910

Difference = 47 × 15 = 705

**∴ The correct answer is ₹705.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of investments of A, B and C = 61 : 43 : 90

Total profit earned at the end of the year = ₹2,910

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Capital × Time

*(Since time is equal for all, Profit Ratio = Capital Ratio)*

 
• 
 
 A (61)
 
 B (43)
 
 C (90)
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Diff = 47
 Total Profit = 194 parts = ₹2,910

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the profits of A, B, and C be 61x, 43x, and 90x respectively.

⇒ Total profit = 61x + 43x + 90x = 194x

⇒ 194x = 2910

⇒ x = 2910 ÷ 194 = 15

⇒ Difference between share of B and C = 90x − 43x = 47x

⇒ Difference = 47 × 15 = 705

**∴ The correct answer is ₹705.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When investments are made for the same time period, profit is shared in the ratio of the invested capitals. (P₁ : P₂ = C₁ : C₂)

Compound Partnership

When investments are for different time periods, profit is shared in the ratio of the product of capital and time. (P₁ : P₂ = C₁ × T₁ : C₂ × T₂)

Working / Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and gets an extra salary or profit percentage. A sleeping partner only invests capital and shares the remaining profit.
